argument:
The bull's Q2 FCF rise to NT$287.36bn from NT$199.85bn strengthens the recurring operating case independently of investment gains. Its 56–58% margin guide is below the peak but above prior-year 49.6%, so a purchase need not assume 60.3% persists. Guidance remains prospective rather than achieved improvement.

Inventory days of 87, overseas execution and Taiwan concentration remain risks even with NT$2,486.33bn liquid surplus and internally funded capex. Cash mitigates financing exposure but cannot diversify geopolitical loss or guarantee marginal fab returns. At 22x forecast earnings, observed growth supplies credible compensation; the 35.31x trailing multiple and RSI near 88 amplify entry sensitivity. I accept a defensible foundry-growth purchase while opposing peak-margin extrapolation and aggressive chasing, not treating normalisation or remaining geopolitical uncertainty as automatic vetoes.
key_points: Growing post-capex cash validates the operating thesis.
Guided normalisation need not erase improved profitability.
Inventory, Taiwan and extended entry still constrain conviction.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers financing capacity and the assumption that peak margin must persist. The surviving counterargument is concentrated geopolitical and capacity-return sensitivity, with extension limiting immediate entry rather than disproving ownership value.
